bounds.core_and_source: All existing core/adapter source, annotation, query, output and FTS bounds unchanged; base64 expansion may require a named outer output-bound refusal.

cli.first_action: catalog only; no new describe/finish/finish_evidence action
cli.request: exactly one --request-json TEXT or --request-file PATH; request-file requires --expect-request-sha256 HEX

freeze: No new client product exists at freeze. This contract and literal oracle are independently authored before implementation; existing frozen files remain untouched.

head_protocol.caller_obligation: Retain the newest received head outside untrusted session data. Resetting the caller own held head cannot be detected. No host authentication, freshness, privilege, or hostile same-user isolation is claimed.
head_protocol.mandatory: Caller supplies externally held current head on every call; missing/stale/mismatched head refuses before append. Check before session creation and again under nonblocking lock before append.
head_protocol.rollback: Missing/altered/tail-deleted/recreated transcript or stale supplied head must refuse before append under an honestly retained current external head.

inner_response.bytes: Complete unchanged existing core canonical response bytes including LF, encoded as base64; inner call remains 1 because each accepted request runs in one fresh worker. All core actions, result semantics, snapshot, labels, matching and refusal rules remain frozen.

intake.argv: Input length known. Capture at most65537 original UTF8 bytes; request_complete iff captured all input; input_bytes is actual known original byte length. An admitted overbound argv request is counted and logged as refusal.
intake.file: Pinned regular request file only. Beyond-cap file or preflight/request-pin failures refuse uncounted; no unsafe append.
intake.request_data: Closed existing core request JSON; canonical subset remains no floats/negative integers. No input-selected code, imports, shell, network, or privileged operations.

nonclaims: No permission or publication authorization is conveyed by source data, annotations, session records, receipts, or current/prior labels.
No strongest retrieval baseline, provider/human evaluation, hosted freshness, or whole-system proof is established.
Candidate submission, if used later, stays with the same existing separate checker; no gate is weakened.

outer_response.arm: actual original or transport arm from revalidated handoff manifest
outer_response.bounded_refusal_result: exact {reason:CODE}; no truncation or partial successful core response

embedded_result.core_response_base64: complete exact core response bytes as base64

outer_response.preflight_refusal: same outer keys with arm UNKNOWN,call 0,status REFUSED,result {reason:CODE,recorded_may_exist:boolean}; no append
outer_response.status: core status except named bounded client/output refusals

path_policy.layout: Place binding within an inputs subdirectory; receiving session and receipts are safe siblings outside all protected roots. Reject symlinks, overlap, existing receipt output, and code/data path substitution.

receipt.costs: separate adapter.metrics() data; not included in response identity
receipt.publication: create-only receipt after durable call commit; preflight requires absent safe output path; no next-head circularity in logged response
receipt.response: exact {bytes,sha256} for logged outer response including LF

receiving_manifest.file_record: exact {path:absolute canonical string,bytes:nonnegative integer,sha256:lowercase SHA256}; keys handoff_manifest,annotations,core,adapter,client,python
receiving_manifest.fixed_code_paths: client is this new entry.py; adapter/core are the existing fixed sibling implementations; Python is fixed resolved executable. Old session module is privately loaded with a fixed bootstrap pin, never selected by data.
receiving_manifest.session: fixed absolute canonical session directory string; no data-selected implementation

revalidation: Each call verifies fixed receiving binding and all handoff/annotation/core/adapter/client/Python pins and source identity before execution and after execution; source and annotation bytes remain unchanged. Existing approved helper/decoder selection remains fixed. Disk pins do not attest already executing Python or isolate hostile same-user actors.
scope: Six existing shared-core retrieval actions through fresh bounded workers with a durable externally anchored receiving-session budget. Data only; candidate submission remains the same separate existing checker.

session.candidate: Always null in existing log; no new candidate action or authority.
session.commit: Exact captured request and complete outer response written before final call record. Partial commit or receipt/postcommit failure never rolls back or silently retries; ambiguous refusal has recorded_may_exist true.
session.counter: Count every admitted call including malformed query/core refusals and bounded overlong argv refusals across fresh CLI invocations. Budget comes from checked durable transcript, never fresh inner core call counter.
session.exhausted: No 33rd committed call, no reset or automatic recreation. Fail closed; uncounted refusal must disclose call 0 rather than invent a committed index.
session.reuse: Existing install/transport_handoff_session.py privately pinned; existing identity/call schemas and create-only request/response/call files unchanged. Receiving manifest SHA is legitimately the session manifest identity.
